pamphlet_excerpts: Silica Dust Control: Wet sponges trap toxic respirable silica dust before particles become airborne hazards.
Kiln Ventilation System: Firing chambers release harmful sulfur dioxide fumes requiring powered exterior canopy hoods.
Mechanical Wheel Guarding: Tie loose hair back so spinning wheelheads cannot snare clothing or cords.
Glaze Chemical Protection: Wear nitrile gloves when weighing toxic raw glaze materials like barium carbonate.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Dust Mitigation: Sponge work tables using clean wet rags to capture settled silica glaze powder.
Step 2 - Ventilation Check: Turn on the mechanical kiln exhaust fan before beginning any heating firing cycle.
Step 3 - Apparel Preparation: Tie long hair back securely and remove all hanging wrist jewelry or rings.
Step 4 - Tool Handling: Store sharp metal carving needles point down inside dedicated sturdy wooden tool blocks.

quiz_item.question: Why should a pottery studio always be cleaned with wet sponges and mops rather than dry sweeping or blowing away dried clay scraps?
options: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.
D. Wet mopping is the only way to dissolve lead oxide out of raw earthenware clay bodies.
choices: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.
D. Wet mopping is the only way to dissolve lead oxide out of raw earthenware clay bodies.
quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Clay and glaze powders contain fine silica particles that stay suspended in the air when dry-swept; wiping surfaces and mopping floors with water traps dust safely.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why should a pottery studio always be cleaned with wet sponges and mops rather than dry sweeping or blowing away dried clay scraps?

B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.
D. Wet mopping is the only way to dissolve lead oxide out of raw earthenware clay bodies.
choices: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Clay and glaze powders contain fine silica particles that stay suspended in the air when dry-swept; wiping surfaces and mopping floors with water traps dust safely.
